subject: External service fingerprinting and egress justification for Private Endpoint integration
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmeedge.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@acmeedge.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Outbound connections - list and service fingerprinting for Private Endpoint

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our network team is ready to onboard Redwood's Private Endpoint but they've asked for tighter evidence before we open outbound firewall rules. Two asks from netsec:

1) A minimal list of FQDNs your runtime will initiate TLS connections to from the control plane / runtime when a customer runs a private deployment.
2) Certificate/TLS fingerprint(s) or a signature bundle we can pin or reference (they prefer cert fingerprint over IP allowlisting where possible).
3) A clear mapping of which hosts are for telemetry, billing/usage, model pulls, and control plane heartbeats, plus ports and protocols.
4) An operations plan for IP rotation: if you rely on IP ranges, how much notice do you provide and can you offer a stable /single-exit-IP option (proxy) for customers who require it?

Attached is a quick scan we ran from our NAT; it has outbound destinations we observed during the POC. Can you review and confirm what each host is used for and whether you can provide stronger artifacts (fingerprints, signed manifest, or guaranteed IP ranges with rotation windows)?

Claire and I need this packaged for our compliance review by Dec 23.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Infrastructure, AcmeEdge

------------------------------------------------------------

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmeedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Outbound connections - list and service fingerprinting for Private Endpoint

Sanjay — thanks for the clear list. We can provide the artifacts you need; below is a compact plan and the immediate next steps.

Summary of egress surfaces (planned for Private deployments):
- controlplane.redwood-inference.com (TLS 443) — control plane RPCs, rollouts, canary traffic; regional variants: us-control.redwood-inference.com
- api.redwood-inference.com (TLS 443) — API calls for hosted/backchannel telemetry and billing submissions
- model-storage.redwood-inference.com (TLS 443) — model pulls / layer downloads (S3-backed); calls may be to regional mirrors in the same FQDN family
- metrics-batch.redwood-inference.com (TLS 443) — telemetry/ops ingest (optional; can be disabled per-tenant)

Ports/protocols: outbound TCP 443 only for all production flows. We do not require non-TLS outbound ports for runtime operation in normal deployments.

Fingerprinting / pinning options we can provide:
- Certificate fingerprint manifest (SHA256) for the leaf certs presented by the endpoints above (attached PDF).
- Signed JSON manifest (HMAC + timestamp) listing FQDN -> cert fingerprint -> service role. Manifest will be rotated at the same cadence as certificates and signed by Redwood's release key.
- Static IP ranges per-region as a fallback: we can provide a set of /24s for US/EU/APAC. We will give 30 days notice for any range changes and publish the change via the Drive link + JIRA ticket.

Operational guarantees and options:
- Default: FQDN + cert fingerprint pinning. This is preferred by netsec teams because it tolerates cloud provider IP churn.
- If a customer requires a single static exit IP, we can route egress through a Redwood-managed egress-proxy for an additional monthly fee and an SLA (single-IP per region).
- For customers that cannot accept TLS-level pinning, we can offer IP-based allowlist with a 30-day rotation window and advance notice in the JIRA ticket.

Deliverables (owners / ETA):
- Cert fingerprints PDF (attached) — owner: Nikhil — ETA: 2026-12-22 15:00Z
- Signed manifest (HMAC + timestamp) — owner: David — ETA: 2026-12-22 15:00Z
- Regional /24 list + rotation policy doc — owner: Marissa — ETA: 2026-12-22 15:00Z
- Example firewall rule snippet and short runbook for your ops team — owner: Marissa — ETA: 2026-12-22 15:00Z

Action for AcmeEdge: please confirm whether you prefer the FQDN+fingerprint path, the static /24 allowlist path, or the egress-proxy path. We'll prioritize the deliverables accordingly.

Regards,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Product Manager — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

--- attachments: cert-fingerprints.pdf (stub) ---
